slides.title: Lost Property Club
items: A return desk for independent hotels.
Illustrative seed pitch

slides.title: Somewhere on this shelf.
items: A guest calls about a hat. The morning desk remembers a hat, but the night desk moved it. A useful answer depends on who picked up the phone.
One shelf record follows the item across shifts.

slides.title: A dent beats a description.
items: Found: green flask
Private detail: crescent dent at the base. Staff log one identifying mark and keep it off the guest-facing notice. The claimant describes it before release.

slides.title: The claim changes hands
items: Reported
Guest records the item, date and a private detail. A reference number works across phone and email.
Matched
Staff compare the description with the shelf record and hold the item while they check ownership.
Returned
A handoff or courier receipt closes the record. The next shift sees who released it and when.

slides.title: One counter, two ways home
items: A guest can collect at the desk with the claim number. For delivery, the desk confirms the address and sends a prepaid shipping link.
The property keeps its own release and retention policy. Staff record exceptions against the item.

slides.title: The desk pays a flat fee
items: per property / month
A hotel gets unlimited staff logins, an item register and a guest claim page. Shipping is passed through at cost.
At $25 in modeled monthly support and hosting, one property contributes $70 before sales and overhead.

slides.title: How much desk time comes back?
items: Minutes per enquiry, modeled front-desk trial
75 enquiries a month × 5 minutes saved gives 6¼ hours back to the desk. Staff time a sample during both shifts before and after rollout.

slides.title: Start with one city’s keys
items: 250 hotels
At $95 per month, 250 subscribing properties represent $285,000 in annual recurring revenue. This is a full-adoption scenario for the initial sales list.
The first introduction
Sell through local hotel operators’ groups. Start with one building and invite its sister properties only after two shifts use the register every day.

slides.title: What a notebook still does well
items: The notebook
It costs almost nothing and stays at the counter. A remote enquiry still requires someone to find the right page and check the shelf.
The shared register
A second property or a night manager can look up the item, see the last action and leave a record for the person who opens the desk tomorrow.

slides.title: Who runs the return desk?
items: June Park
Hotel operations. June owns property onboarding, shelf labels and the release checklist used by desk staff.
Omar Bell
Product engineering. Omar owns claim matching, staff access and the activity record that carries across shifts.

slides.title: Thirty desks in twelve months
items: First 5
Pilot for six weeks. Measure time per enquiry and check unclaimed items against the physical shelf.
Next 10
Charge the monthly fee and document the first successful handover across sister properties.
Final 15
Train via the property manager. Seek paid renewals from four of the original five pilots.

slides.title: Return to sender.
items: $480k pre-seed
$210k builds the product, $150k funds hotel onboarding and $120k runs support and field trials. The twelve-month target is 30 paying properties.
